memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'These are the words you are to speak to the Israelites.' So Moses went back and
summoned the elders of the people and set before them all the words the LORD had
commanded him to speak. The people all responded together, 'We will do everything
the LORD has said.' So Moses brought their answer back to the LORD."
- Ex 19:6b-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"We will do everything the LORD has said." All of them, together, without
hesitation.

They meant it. There is no reason to doubt their sincerity in this moment. They
had seen the sea open and the manna fall, and their hearts were full.

And within forty days they would be dancing around a golden calf.

We should not read that with contempt, because we recognise it. Sincere promises
made in moments of spiritual clarity have a way of dissolving under pressure.
Peter told Jesus he would never disown Him, and he meant every word (Matt
26:35).

Here is what this reveals, and it is the deep problem the whole Bible addresses:
sincerity is not the same as ability. Israel genuinely wanted to obey and
genuinely could not. Willing hearts in that moment; unchanged hearts underneath.

Which is exactly why God later promises something better: "I will give you a new
heart and put a new spirit in you... and move you to follow my decrees"
(Ezek 36:26-27). Not better instructions. A new heart.

That promise is fulfilled in Christ, who does not merely tell us what to do but
gives us His Spirit to do it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you sincerely promised God and failed to keep?
2. Do you rely on your willpower or on the Spirit's work in you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, my intentions are better than my performance. Thank You for the new heart
You give and the Spirit who works in me. Amen.
